sentences.t: The founding idea was not lending.
Indiafintech's read of the draft prospectus is that the app started as a personal finance tracker, a tool to log spending and watch a credit score.
Over a decade that gave Moneyview something lenders usually pay for: a large base of people who already share their financial data and who first came for something free.
The company's description of itself in the prospectus, per Oquilia, is a "consumer-focused, digital-only, credit-led financial services platform for Middle India".
The personal loan product launched in 2017 (Economic Times).
The company converted to a public limited company in June 2025 ahead of the IPO (Inc42).
The why of the model is a funnel.
Of 125.49 million registered users at 31 December 2025, 9.73 million, or 7.75%, had used a revenue-generating product, up from 3.64% in FY23 (Indiafintech).
At 30 June 2026 the figures were 140.28 million and 11.90 million, which is 8.5% (RHP via Oquilia, share calculated here).
Indiafintech's point is that each extra percentage point of conversion is about 1.25 million more paying users, at close to zero acquisition cost because they are already in the app.
The ticket size is small.

Indiafintech, quoting the draft prospectus, says loans under ₹1 lakh have grown 48 times since 2017, with non-bank lenders and fintechs holding 82% of that segment, and that digital loans were 13% of unsecured personal loan sanctions in FY25.
The Economic Times reports Moneyview was about 11% of digital unsecured personal loan sanctions that year.
The average user earns ₹47,000 a month and is 32 (Economic Times).
The income mix has shifted.
Fees and commission, which Moneyview earns for originating loans that other lenders fund, were 87.9% of revenue in FY23 and 55.5% in the nine months to December 2025.
Interest income went from 6.6% to 38.8% (Indiafintech).
Moneyview is turning from a seller of loans into a holder of loans.
Holding a loan earns interest for years, but it needs capital behind it.
Moneyview lends through its own non-bank subsidiary, Whizdm Finance, alongside banks and other lenders.
Under Reserve Bank of India rules, middle-layer non-bank lenders must hold capital equal to 15% of their risk-weighted assets (Medianama).
The subsidiary disbursed ₹5,429.6 crore in the nine months to December 2025 (Medianama).
The draft prospectus planned ₹450 crore of the fresh issue to strengthen the subsidiary's capital (Medianama, Inc42).

On the loans it does not hold, Moneyview takes part of the credit risk through a default loss guarantee (DLG, a promise to cover a lender's first losses on a loan pool), up to 5% of the portfolio under the Reserve Bank's rules.
At 31 December 2025 it had facilitated ₹9,165.7 crore of loans under these arrangements, and DLG expense was ₹318.8 crore, 15.3% of total expenses (Medianama).
The draft prospectus planned ₹650 crore of the ₹1,500 crore fresh issue to fund DLG cover (Inc42).
The issue that listed was smaller.
The final prospectus of 28 September offered a fresh issue of ₹750 crore plus a sale of 10.05 crore existing shares, about ₹342 crore at ₹34, for ₹1,091.68 crore in total (Prospectus, Oquilia).
The split between uses was set in the draft; the final allocation is in the prospectus.
Total income went from ₹1,389.24 crore in FY24 to ₹2,378.53 crore in FY25 and ₹3,404.27 crore in FY26, up 43% in the last year (RHP via Oquilia).
Restated profit barely moved: Medianama reports ₹240.3 crore for FY25, and the prospectus figure for FY26 is ₹242.71 crore.
Two items fall in FY26.
Indiafintech counts an exceptional loss from the August 2025 cyber incident, and a ₹160 crore one-time incentive approved for the chief executive in March 2026.
Then the June 2026 quarter showed total income of ₹1,065.09 crore and profit of ₹173.80 crore, which is 72% of the full FY26 profit in one quarter (RHP via Oquilia).
Concentration eased.
The top 10 financial partners were 37.31% of revenue in the nine months to December 2025, against 46.82% in FY25 (Medianama).
Those partners are not exclusive and can leave for a rival.
Asset quality.
Indiafintech's read of the draft prospectus is that gross stage 3 loans, the bucket for credit-impaired loans, rose from 0.94% to 2.53% over 18 months.
It calls that manageable at this ticket size, and says the direction matters more than the level.
Regulation.
Moneyview's prospectus says repeated Reserve Bank action on DLG caps, buy-now-pay-later rules and outsourcing of lending functions is a risk to its model (Medianama).
In February 2026 the Reserve Bank restored the DLG framework for non-bank lenders after curbs the year before had forced higher provisions (Medianama).
Security.
In August 2025 Whizdm Finance was hit by a cyber attack through an interface with partner banks, with unauthorised withdrawals from its accounts.
Medianama puts the loss at ₹48.3 crore.
Indiafintech puts it at ₹469.99 million, about ₹47 crore, or ₹35.17 crore after tax.
Both are reading the same disclosure, and this read gives both figures.
The issue ran from 24 to 28 September at ₹32 to ₹34 and was subscribed 98.46 times.
Qualified institutional buyers bid 227.45 times their portion, non-institutional investors 115.41 times, and retail investors 19.57 times (CNBC-TV18, NSE data).
The shares opened at ₹55 on the NSE on 1 October, 61.76% over the issue price.
The close on 12 October was ₹62.12, 82.7% above it, and the stock traded near ₹61.38 on Tuesday (Mint).

Sellers in the offer included both founders, who each offered 13,548,300 shares, about ₹46 crore each at ₹34, at weighted average costs of 34 paise and 74 paise a share, plus Accel, Ribbit Capital and other investors (Prospectus).
This section is analysis built on the facts above and today's paper.
Moneyview launched credit cards, earned wage access, insurance, digital gold and UPI payments only from August 2024, and Indiafintech calls the non-lending products nascent.
The company's prospectus risk list notes that the wider product range brings it under IRDAI and SEBI scrutiny (Medianama).
IRDAI's reform paper targets distributors' commissions and expenses, and a member said on 12 October that caps could start on 1 January 2027 (see the morning paper).
The company's income is mainly loans, so the direct exposure to insurance commission caps is limited, and the loans business sits under the Reserve Bank, not IRDAI.
What to watch.
The share of loans on its own books against loans it only originates, DLG expense as a share of total expenses, gross stage 3 loans, and the share of registered users who pay.
